questions.question: Which event transformed English from Old English to Middle English?
questions.explanation: The Norman Conquest brought massive French influence, transforming English into Middle English (1100-1500).

questions.question: Who brought the language that became Old English to Britain?
options: Germanic tribes — the Angles, Saxons and Jutes — around 450 AD
questions.explanation: English originated with Germanic tribes who invaded Britain around 450 AD.

questions.question: Which word origin pattern is correct?
options: Anglo-Saxon words are basic and everyday; French words are formal; Latin words are technical
French words are basic; Anglo-Saxon words are technical
Latin words are everyday; Anglo-Saxon words are scientific
All English words come from one source
questions.explanation: Anglo-Saxon gave basic words (heart, home), French gave formal terms (government, cuisine), Latin gave technical terms (demonstrate).

questions.question: How did Middle English change compared to Old English?
options: Grammar was simplified while vocabulary expanded massively
The language lost most of its vocabulary
questions.explanation: Middle English simplified the inflected Old English grammar while absorbing thousands of French words.

questions.question: Why does English have synonym pairs like "kingly" and "royal"?
options: It absorbed words for the same concept from multiple languages
questions.explanation: English uniquely has synonyms from multiple sources (Anglo-Saxon, French, Latin), creating richness and nuance.
